title: Case split on sigma <= 3/2 to glue a strip bound and a half-plane bound
intent: Bound |ζ'/ζ(σ+it)| uniformly by a single C·log²|t| over the whole region σ ≥ 1 − F/log|t| by combining two regional bounds that meet at σ = 3/2 — the strip bound (valid for 1 − F/log|t| ≤ σ ≤ 3/2) and the half-plane bound (valid for σ ≥ 3/2) — taking C = max C1 C2 and splitting on σ ≤ 3/2.
also_known_as: gluing two regional bounds at a boundary

parent.name: LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBound
parent.statement:
theorem LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBound : ∃ (C : ℝ) (_ : 0 < C),
    ∀ (σ t : ℝ), 3 < |t| → σ ∈ Set.Ici (1 - F / Real.log |t|) →
      ‖ζ' (σ + t * I) / ζ (σ + t * I)‖ ≤ C * Real.log |t| ^ (2 : ℝ)

children.name: LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBoundStripSpec
children.statement:
lemma LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBoundStripSpec : ∃ (C : ℝ) (_ : 0 < C),
    ∀ (t : ℝ), 3 ≤ |t| →
      ∀ (σ : ℝ), σ ∈ Set.Icc (1 - F / Real.log |t|) (3 / 2) →
          ‖ζ' (σ + t * I) / ζ (σ + t * I)‖ ≤ C * (Real.log |t|) ^ 2
children.closed_by: LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBoundStrip.choose_spec.2 (the second projection of the witness chosen from LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBoundStrip, lines 2603-2752)

children.name: LogDerivZetaBdd_of_Re_ge_three_halves
children.statement:
lemma LogDerivZetaBdd_of_Re_ge_three_halves :
    ∃ C, ∀ (s : ℂ), 3/2 ≤ s.re → ‖deriv riemannZeta s / riemannZeta s‖ ≤ C
children.closed_by: a 32-line proof (lines 2786-2817) via vonMangoldtLSeriesSummable and LogDerivativeDirichlet, ending with `simpa [neg_div, h_log_deriv_sum s hs] using (h_triangle s).trans (hSum.tsum_le_tsum (fun n ↦ h_norm_summand s hs n) h_sum_converges)`

applicability.goal_shape: a goal `∃ C > 0, ∀ x, P x → Q x ≤ C · g x` whose region `P x` is the union of two sub-regions split at a boundary `b` (here `1 - F/log|t| ≤ σ` split at `σ = 3/2`), with a named lemma already bounding `Q x` on each sub-region with the same gauge `g`
applicability.use_when: two proved lemmas bound the same quantity on regions that meet at a common boundary so their union is the goal's domain; the boundary is a linear inequality (`σ ≤ 3/2`) that `by_cases` decides; both lemmas use the same gauge, or the weaker gauge is dominated by it (here the constant bound is dominated by log²|t| for |t| > 3)
applicability.avoid_when: the two regions leave a gap that must also be proved; the two lemmas use different gauges with no domination; the boundary is not an order on a linear-ordered type; or one lemma's constant cannot be carried into the other's region

claims.claim: The parent LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBound is assembled in its proof body (lines 2834-2850) from exactly two named project lemmas — LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBoundStripSpec (line 2834) and LogDerivZetaBdd_of_Re_ge_three_halves (line 2835) — by `use max C1 C2` and a `by_cases hσ' : σ ≤ 3/2` split, with each branch closing by one `.trans` to the child's bound.

Neither the parent nor its two children rest on a hole: StrongPNT.lean contains no `sorry`, `admit` or `axiom` (the only line mentioning 'axioms' is the diagnostic `#print axioms StrongPNT` at line 2906).

claims.claim: The authors state the glue's plan in one sentence in the blueprint annotation — 'Put the previous two Lemmas together.' (lines 2828-2830) — and the half-plane child's plan as the Dirichlet-series bound '... ≤ Σ Λ(n)/n^(3/2) < ∞ by vonMangoldtLSeriesSummable' (lines 2777-2782).

The main proof is 17 lines (2834-2850) and combines 2 direct project lemmas; the strip child's proof is 1 line (2765) and the half-plane child's is 32 lines (2786-2817); the checked chain below the parent is depth 3 (parent → StripSpec → LogDerivZetaUniformLogSquaredBoundStrip → SumBoundII).

consequences: Creates two goals by `by_cases hσ' : σ ≤ 3/2`, whose exhaustiveness is discharged by the law of the excluded middle (no separate exhaustiveness child, unlike a finite `rcases` disjunction). Both branches must close against the same witness `max C1 C2`, so each needs a `le_max_left`/`le_max_right` step, and the weaker (constant) half-plane bound must be shown `≤ C · log²|t|`; here that means proving `1 ≤ log²|t|` from `3 < |t|` via `Real.exp_one_lt_d9`. Failure mode: if the two gauges did not dominate one another, the `gcongr`/`nth_rewrite` normalisation would not close, and a third lemma or a different split point would be needed.
